headline: Biofuels policy clarity drives a raised earnings outlook
summary_short: ADM reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $20.49B (+1.6% y/y) and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.62 (+2% y/y), as adjusted EPS of $0.71 absorbed $275M of net negative mark-to-market and timing impacts tied to strengthening biofuels margins.
summary_long: Revenue rose 10.4% q/q and 1.6% y/y to $20.49B. GAAP EPS fell 34% q/q but rose 2% y/y to $0.62, as $275M of net negative mark-to-market and timing impacts hit Ag Services & Oilseeds — Crushing fell $126M y/y — amid a strengthening biofuels margin environment following U.S. RVO policy clarity. Carbohydrate Solutions profit rose 48% y/y to $356M on ethanol margins; Nutrition rose 42% y/y to $135M on Flavors strength and Decatur East recovery. Cash fell to $591M (from $1.02B q/q); long-term debt fell to $6.46B. ADM raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.15–$4.70 (from $3.60–$4.25) and held capex guidance at $1.3–$1.5B.

drivers.explanation: Growth was supported by higher AS&O export volumes (soybean, sorghum, corn) and stronger Carbohydrate Solutions ethanol margins amid U.S. biofuels policy clarity from the finalized 2026-2027 RVOs.
GAAP EPS rose modestly y/y as $275M of net negative mark-to-market and timing impacts in AS&O (mostly Crushing) were offset by 48% y/y growth in Carbohydrate Solutions and 42% in Nutrition.
Net earnings rose slightly y/y despite AS&O's mark-to-market drag, as Carbohydrate Solutions ethanol strength and Nutrition's Flavors/Decatur East recovery offset the decline.
Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.15-$4.70 (from $3.60-$4.25), citing sustained biofuels policy clarity and expected improvement in crushing and ethanol earnings.
